heading: Publication

calibration.note: Same inherited one-paper calibration (rhgrh100 length table and sentence sample); no new measurement was made for this problem. The rules are restated for a two-conclusion estimate proof with one auxiliary construction (the primitive) and one cited principle (Hölder on the window).

rules.rule: No sentence may be commentary only. A reason for a step may appear only as a clause of the sentence that takes the step.
No restatement of the claim before the derivation; the proof opens with its first step and the statement is carried by the closing sentence.

The Hölder step on the window is invoked in one sentence that says what it consumes (the window-measure bound) and what it returns; finiteness and atomlessness of the restricted measure, which make the primitive continuous, are clauses and not separate checks.
At most 168 words; aim for 120 or fewer.
Every mandatory node of the content plan is realized or merged with an honest quote; every dependency between nodes in the alignment is still visible in the prose.
rules.from: programme gate for P3 and P4

nodes.reason: PR2; the closing sentence states both conclusions.
The restricted-measure reading in one sentence, as the opening step.
L^p inside L^1 on a finite measure is a clause of the sentence that introduces the primitive (PR3).
The window-measure bound in one sentence, as the clause Hölder consumes.
The primitive, with finiteness and atomlessness as clauses (PR3).
The interval identity and continuity of the numerator.
One sentence applying Hölder on the window and saying what it consumes (PR3).
The conclusion sentence with the constant and its validity for every real t.
Combine the two conclusions; carries the statement of the result (PR2).

window-near-endpoint.reason: The opening sentence says the window contributes its part inside the interval, which is the zero-extension reading as a clause.

continuity-from-integrability.reason: PR3 makes the primitive sentence name finiteness (hence L^1) and atomlessness as the clauses behind its continuity.

why-not-symmetric-difference.reason: A paper does not contrast its route with the one it did not take.

bound-needs-no-t-restriction.reason: The conclusion sentence records that the estimate holds for every real t, as a clause.

why-this-constant.reason: The constant is named as the dual norm of the normalised window indicator in the clause of the concluding estimate.

note: Question decisions differ from the expert-reference profile in three places: the window reading, the primitive's hypotheses and the constant are anticipated here because PR1 and PR3 fold reasons into the step sentences; the symmetric-difference contrast is omitted as commentary on a road not taken.
